stories.w: Today is the first Vermont Libraries Day, a new annual statewide observance the Legislature created this spring as Act 127. State Librarian Catherine Delneo says the best way to mark it is to go, whether that means signing up for a library card, checking out a book, taking part in a program or borrowing a museum or state park pass. stories.t: Vermont will restore fire towers on Spruce and Elmore mountains using helicopters this fall
stories.w: The state is replacing the steep and sometimes rickety wooden staircases on the Elmore and Spruce fire towers with metal steps and railings like the ones at Allis State Park, and because both summits are so high and remote, a helicopter will carry up roughly 3,000 pounds of materials. stories.t: OnLogic to Be Acquired for $675 Million by Omron, a Japanese Firm
stories.w: Omron, a Kyoto automation company with 26,000 employees, is buying the South Burlington computer hardware maker that Roland and Lisa Groeneveld started at their kitchen table in 2003 as Logic Supply, and the deal is expected to close in January. stories.w: A month after Vermont's first diverging diamond opened in Colchester on Sept. 17, the overall message from drivers is positive, though some say the new signals have made their commute worse and the cones are still out. stories.w: A pilot program would let licensed cannabis retailers sell from a sanctioned area at events like concerts, farmers markets and sporting events, though nobody could consume on site. Growers and shops say it would help in a market made up of some 300 small cultivators, where a storefront is often too expensive and strict advertising rules make it hard to get the word out. stories.w: A lawsuit filed this month in Chittenden Superior Court says two Winooski officers broke Marc White's neck, ankle, hand and two fingers while taking him down in his apartment building's vestibule in February 2025, then told EMTs the blood on his face came from a fall on the sidewalk. stories.w: Students at UVM and Middlebury are running voter registration drives ahead of the Nov. 3 election, with UVM's helping classmates request absentee ballots, and UVM's nonpartisan Political Science Club says attendance is picking up again after falling off following 2024. stories.t: Vermonters Will Vote on Two Constitutional Amendments This Fall
stories.w: On Nov. 3, Vermonters get the final say on two constitutional amendments, confusingly numbered Proposal 3 and Proposal 4, after two rounds of lawmakers signed off. Proposal 3 would guarantee workers the right to join a union and block any future right to work law, which Rep. In the lobby, Moss Café + Bar does espresso, pastries and grab and go sandwiches and salads by day, then wine, beer and cocktails with small bites at night, while the 75 seat Treetops restaurant on the eighth floor serves breakfast and dinner, with 40 outdoor seat

stories.t: Construction begins on new affordable housing in Burlington
stories.w: Champlain Housing Trust broke ground Friday on the Shale Beach Condominiums, 30 permanently affordable homes in the Cambrian Rise neighborhood of the New North End, with the two and three bedroom units expected to sell for $175,000 to $210,000. Under the trust's shared equity model, buyers purchase the home while the trust keeps the land, and when they sell they split the appreciation with the tru

stories.w: Democratic nominee Amanda Janoo, an economist from Burlington, wants a 2% surcharge on personal income over $250,000 and an 8% surcharge on income over $500,000, which Fair Share for Vermont estimates would raise $344 million a year, with the money going toward free primary and preventive care for every Vermonter. stories.t: General election ballots mailed out to Vermont voters
stories.w: You can also drop your ballot at your town clerk's office during business hours, or in an official drop box any time before Election Day on Nov. 3. Voting in person still works too, either with your mailed ballot or with a new one at the polls, and anyone who hasn't received a ballot by mid October should contact their town clerk.

stories.w: Sen. Bernie Sanders endorsed Amanda Janoo for governor on Wednesday in a video statement, saying he personally likes Gov. Phil Scott but backs Janoo's plans for free primary and preventive care, lower property taxes paid for by luxury second homes and large corporate investors, and a statewide moratorium on AI data centers. Janoo said the two met about two weeks earlier for a "great, nerdy policy

stories.t: Vermont Legal Aid program to fight eviction may end due to lost funding
stories.w: Vermont Legal Aid's tenant representation pilot put a team of four attorneys on eviction cases starting in November 2024 and has opened and closed 207 cases, 54 of them for tenants over 60. It ends Oct. 31 because the state isn't replenishing the just over $1 million it got through Act 47, the Vermont Home Act of 2023. stories.t: Benefit concert brings Make-A-Wish families and jam band fans together in South Burlington
stories.w: The Wish Benefit Tour's sold out stop at Higher Ground on Wednesday paired Dead & Company founding member Oteil Burbridge with Vermont groove trio LaMP, with all proceeds going to Make-A-Wish chapters in Vermont, Northeast New York, Massachusetts and Rhode Island. stories.t: Gov. Scott swaps EV for hybrid, cites charging struggles
stories.w: Four years after becoming the first governor in the country to use an electric vehicle as his official state vehicle, Gov. Phil Scott disclosed last week that he gave up his Ford Lightning last fall, after putting about 70,000 miles on it, because charging stations were too hard to find on the road. He's driving a hybrid now and says he'll get another EV once the technology and the charging networ

stories.t: Despite some overall progress, Vermont test scores show a widening achievement gap
stories.w: The state's first look at 2025-26 test results shows the proficiency gap between marginalized students and their peers now runs 30 to 38 percentage points, up from 26 to 36 last year, with the widest gap in sixth grade English language arts. The state counts students with disabilities, living in poverty, from racial or ethnic minorities and several other groups as marginalized, and they make up 57

stories.t: GlobalFoundries brings massive solar array, battery storage online in Essex Junction
stories.w: GlobalFoundries switched on a new solar array and a 16 megawatt battery storage system at its Essex Junction campus last Monday, with the panels covering more than 30 acres of underused land that includes an old parking lot and a brownfield. stories.t: Emerald ash borer has arrived in Charlotte, found at Mt. Philo
stories.w: The state's invasive species coordinator has confirmed the first emerald ash borer detection in Charlotte, at Mount Philo State Park. The beetle's larvae feed under ash bark and girdle the tree, and the most definitive sign is small, D shaped exit holes in the trunk, along with thinning leaves, vertical bark splits and extra woodpecker activity. stories.t: South Burlington couple loses home in fast-moving fire
stories.w: Stephen Snook and his wife were watching the Yankees game in the basement of their Butler Drive home last Wednesday night when the fire started, and within minutes flames were shooting out of the windows. stories.t: ‘You can’t lose things like this’: Barre community rallies in attempt to save ice rink
stories.w: About a week after Barre announced that the piping in its 52 year old BOR Arena was full of leaks and the rink likely wouldn't open this winter, local tradespeople started volunteering to try a fix. Heating installer Ed Patterson, whose son is a senior on the Spaulding High School hockey team, came up with a plan to reinforce the failed system with plastic tubing, and almost a dozen volunteers are

stories.t: Burlington seeks input on park playground renovations
stories.w: Burlington Parks wants to give the playgrounds at Baird, Ethan Allen and Smalley parks the same accessible equipment Pomeroy Park got when it reopened in July, at around $200,000 per park, with help from the Parks Foundation's Playgrounds for All Forever campaign. stories.t: Familiar faces from Norman Rockwell’s paintings visit Shelburne Museum
stories.w: Norman Rockwell lived in Arlington for 14 years, creating more than 175 Saturday Evening Post covers there and famously paying his neighbors $5 and a cold Coca-Cola to model. Burlington radio station celebrates 80 years on air
stories.w: WJOY began broadcasting in 1946 and moved to its current home on Joy Drive in South Burlington in 1967. On Thursday the station marked 80 years by inviting listeners in to reminisce, and host Ginny McGehee was there to celebrate with them. Happy 80th, WJOY!

stories.t: One Dish: Sabah’s House Shares Shawarma From a Family Recipe
stories.w: Mustafa Khudaier, 19, reopened the city owned kiosk at the corner of Church and College streets in late June as Sabah's House, the spot Leunig's used to run as Petit Bijou, and his mother, Sabah Abbas, is the one with the recipes. stories.t: Governor proposes funding Burlington shelter with overdose center money
stories.w: Speaking in Rutland on Wednesday, Gov. Phil Scott suggested moving the money set aside for Burlington's proposed overdose prevention center toward the low barrier, 100 bed shelter for chronically homeless people that city and business leaders keep calling for. stories.w: More than two years after a 2024 law cleared the way for it, the center still hasn't opened, and the city has signed a letter of intent on a building while declining to say even which neighborhood it's in. stories.t: Police face barrage of questions but provide few answers about shooting by Williston officer
stories.w: Around 4:50 Thursday morning, a man drove up to Williston officers who were dealing with downed wires across Route 2A, and one of them shot him in the hip. The man has since been released from the hospital, the road reopened around 4 that afternoon, and two officers are on paid administrative leave while state police investigate. At Thursday's press conference, police said they still had to review

stories.t: 'Tailgate party for birders' will commence in Huntington this weekend
stories.w: The Birds of Vermont Museum in Huntington hosts its 12 hour Big Sit! on Sunday from 6 AM to 6 PM, with birders camped in a 17 foot circle counting every species they spot. The international event started in New Haven, Connecticut, in 1992, the museum has hosted its own circle since 2003, and donations are pledged based on how many species turn up. stories.t: Parents of cyclist who was killed in crosswalk file wrongful death lawsuit against driver
stories.w: Shiloh Skalka, 16, a Burlington High School student, was killed on her e-bike in the crosswalk at Pine and Locust streets on July 16, and her parents are now suing driver Douglas Knapp, the 80 year old folk artist known as dug Nap, for unspecified damages. The suit says the crossing's warning lights had been flashing for 7 seconds when the crash happened, and police estimated he was driving 28 mph

stories.t: Beware of were-hens: Vermont theater company launches successful Halloween show
stories.w: Hatchford Hotel is an original Halloween musical comedy written by Greg Skillman and Adam Rabin, and it's only the second musical the Shelburne Players have staged in their 24 years. The show heads into its second weekend with this weekend's performances almost sold out, though there is a waitlist.

stories.t: Valcour Island’s Unknown Soldiers Are Finally Laid to Rest
stories.w: The gunboat Philadelphia sank at the Battle of Valcour Island in 1776 and stayed on the bottom of Lake Champlain until diver Lorenzo Hagglund found the wreck in 1935, and teeth recovered with it will now be buried with full military honors. stories.t: Festivities underway for 250th anniversary of the Battle of Valcour
stories.w: Sunday marks 250 years since the battle, and Plattsburgh's one time weekend of events runs Friday through Sunday. The highlight is Sunday's reenactment with replica boats on Lake Champlain, staged off Plattsburgh City Beach so it's easier to watch, with more than 100 reenactors from as far as Ohio and Virginia, and a memorial service closes out the weekend.

stories.t: Anti-ICE activists plan week of community engagement, learning and protest

stories.w: Vermont National Guard Commander Maj. Gen. Hank Harder told WCAX that the Green Mountain Boys were tasked with taking out Iranian air defenses during their recent Middle East deployment and came under attack, though the Guard took no casualties. stories.t: Medicaid Changes Are Set to Kick In for Vermonters
stories.w: An estimated 235 Vermonters were expected to lose Medicaid on October 1 over restrictions tied to immigration status, the first wave of changes from the federal budget law President Donald Trump signed last year, and starting January 1, work requirements and twice yearly reviews phase in for an estimated 49,000 low income adults as they renew. Younger Vermonters are hit hardest, with 27% of those 18 to 44 struggling compared with 9% of people over 65. stories.t: Burlington YMCA property redevelopment moves one step closer to new housing
stories.w: Green Castle Group's Bruce Baker is turning the old downtown Y, vacant from 2019 until construction began in 2025, into 79 apartments from studios to four bedrooms, each with its own heating and cooling, plus a 24 hour gym, balconies and community spaces. stories.t: Vermont’s Housing Market Has Tilted Back Toward Buyers, But Only a Certain Kind
stories.w: The Vermont Association of Realtors counted nearly 3,000 active listings statewide last month, the most since 2020, and the median home now spends 17 days on the market, up from a low of 6 in 2022, so even in Chittenden County homes with more than a few offers are the exception. stories.w: A Vermont Public poll found 57% approve of taxing second homes and 28% oppose, and Democrat Amanda Janoo says the tax could free up housing for Vermonters, with the highest rates aimed at private equity and large corporate owners. stories.t: Winooski multiyear revitalization project complete as Main Street officially reopens
stories.w: Winooski cut the ribbon Wednesday on nearly 4,000 feet of rebuilt Main Street, running from the railroad bridge near Maple Street out to the Colchester line, after more than two years of construction and detours. Michael Henry spent almost nine hours of one day in the break room, then approached the officer who reported him, and a third investigation found he'd been overpaid more than $50,000 in the last year. stories.t: Officials pick new possible spot for OD Prevention Center
stories.w: Burlington and Vermonters for Criminal Justice Reform signed a letter of intent to buy a property for Vermont's first overdose prevention center, which keeps it off the market for 90 days, CEDO director Kara Alnasrawi told the City Council Monday. stories.w: Rep. Troy Headrick of Burlington and members of the Odanak First Nation from Quebec were hosting a private presentation on Abenaki heritage with UVM historians and students when members of the Abenaki Nation of Missisquoi showed up, and the Odanak council says one person was arrested and released. stories.t: In a surprise move, Vermont's Roman Catholic Diocese seeks to dismiss its 2-year-old bankruptcy case
stories.w: Two years and $2 million in legal fees into its Chapter 11 case, the diocese asked the court Wednesday to dismiss it, after creditors including more than 100 abuse claimants turned down a $29.4 million settlement offer that would average $247,000 per claimant. stories.t: Gov. Scott sends letter to president pushing for more refugees in Vermont
stories.w: Gov. Phil Scott wrote to President Trump on Thursday asking the administration to increase and broaden refugee admissions for next year. Vermont is set to welcome about 125 refugees in the next fiscal year, but Scott says the state has the capacity for up to 300, and he made a similar request back in 2020.

stories.t: Poll shows majority of Vermonters disapprove of ICE enforcement actions
stories.w: In the new Vermont Public poll, 62% of respondents disapprove of how ICE is enforcing immigration laws, 54% strongly, while 25% strongly approve, and the split runs deep along party lines with 89% of Democrats strongly disapproving and 65% of Republicans strongly approving. stories.t: ICE Surge Is Targeting Vermont's Roofing and Construction Workers
stories.w: Mary Richards of Cornwall spent three years looking for someone to replace her leaking slate roof, and on the crew's second day in August, ICE agents detained two roofers from a South Burlington company in less than 10 minutes. stories.t: Burlington High School class of 1966 tours new BHS
stories.w: The Class of 1966 was only the second to graduate from the old North Avenue building, and a reunion this weekend brought them back to tour the new BHS standing where it used to be. stories.t: Federal grants invigorate efforts to address veteran homelessness in Vermont
stories.w: The VA awarded $18,499,223 to organizations across Vermont and New Hampshire that house and support veterans, part of $1.17 billion going to 680 groups nationwide. stories.w: Vermont raised the income limits for its Medicare Savings Program, which helps seniors pay Medicare premiums and sometimes co-pays and deductibles, and nearly 12,000 Vermonters have already enrolled. stories.t: A celebration of 'maple-fired' punk highlights challenging times for Vermont's live music
stories.w: Randolph's brand new Skunkfest was set for Saturday outside The Underground with nine punk and ska bands, a makers' market and a fixer tent, but owner Vincent Freeman says the venue's regular shows go on indefinite hiatus by the end of the year after his insurer dropped him and music licensing costs added up. stories.t: 'Mend it and keep it alive': Inside Vermont's growing repair culture
stories.w: Every third Saturday, volunteers at the Old North End Repair Cafe at 12-22 North Street fix one another's broken belongings over bagels, and it is one of the spots listed in ReuseVT, a new state funded directory of repair cafes, repair businesses and lending libraries. Director Susan Alexander says the hard part is economics, since a $27 toaster online can beat a $35 fix from the guy down the road

stories.w: The Bidwell opened in June in the former Stowe Street Café space in Waterbury, and every dish and drink is available all day, from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. Co-owner Rachael Brown, most recently of Prohibition Pig, wrote a wine list that describes bottles through TV characters from Schitt's Creek, Firefly and Gilmore Girls, while chef Tiffany Caldwell, formerly Heirloom Hospitality's commissary chef, turns
